groups.sentence: Instructors may use AI to draft and refine course materials such as syllabi, lesson plans, rubrics, quiz questions and assignments.
AI uses for instructors include building materials, assessments, tutors and grading help, without requiring them.
Instructors may use AI to translate course materials or convert them into other formats for diverse learners.
Instructors do not rely on AI alone to produce whole courses or critical course content.
Instructors may use approved AI tools to draft feedback on student work, give an initial review, or score against a rubric.
Instructors review AI output and remain responsible for the final teaching product.
Instructors may use AI to draft course announcements, emails and other communications with students.
Teaching assistants and staff use AI only as their supervisors and the instructor allow.
Instructors use AI to enhance teaching and save time.
Instructors do not let AI replace their own teaching, expertise or professional judgment.
Instructors use AI ethically and in line with institutional standards, and departments discuss acceptable uses.
Automating teaching, feedback or reporting with AI raises concerns and should not rest on AI output alone.
Instructors may choose not to use AI.
